groups.title: [CRITICAL] Optics: pi phase counted twice in Airy reflectance inverts every interference fringe
groups.summary:
The interference LUT generator, both bubble shaders and the CPU reference add pi (lambda/2) to the phase before evaluating the Airy reflectance `F sin^2(phi/2) / (1 + F sin^2(phi/2))`. For a free-standing film (air|film|air) the Airy form already contains the reflection phase flip through `r21 = -r12`, so the extra pi turns `sin^2` into `cos^2`: every fringe is inverted. A zero-thickness film is maximally bright instead of black, and a quarter-wave film is black instead of brightest. This affects the default render on every frame.

Lead re-check (exact complex-amplitude slab reflectance vs the code's formula, n = 1.33, lambda = 532 nm):

| d (nm) | exact | code (+pi) | without +pi |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.00000 | 0.07711 | 0.00000 |
| 100 | 0.07711 | 0.00000 | 0.07711 |
| 200 | 0.00000 | 0.07711 | 0.00000 |

`git log -S` shows the shader's `wavelength + pi` arriving in 4fef328 (2026-01-21); it was carried into the LUT in 21747d7. A hard 30 nm black-film cutoff in the shaders hides the d -> 0 symptom, and existing tests check only value ranges.
acceptance: `+ PI` removed at `src/render/interference_lut.rs:68`, `+ pi` removed at `src/render/shaders/bubble.wgsl:464` and `src/render/shaders/bubble_instanced.wgsl:208`, and the `+ lambda/2` removed from the path difference fed to the Airy formula in `src/physics/interference.rs`
Unit tests assert Airy reflectance is 0 at d = 0 and maximal at d = lambda / (4 n cos(theta_t)), and that the implementation matches an exact complex-amplitude slab reference
Golden images in `tests/golden` regenerated and visually reviewed
All tests pass

groups.title: [HIGH] Drainage: GPU solver never advances (dt not uploaded, f32 underflow, stale accessor)
groups.summary: `GPUDrainageSimulator::step` computes `step_dt` but only adds it to `current_time`; `set_dt` has no callers, so the shader integrates with the default `dt = 0.001` s forever. At h = 500 nm the per-step change is about 0.007 ulp in f32 and a uniform initial field has zero Laplacian, so the thickness buffer stays exactly uniform. The time-scale slider changes only the displayed clock (about 167x off at 60 fps). Branched-flow GRIN bending and the caustics pass therefore read a flat field. Related defects: the GPU pole rows are frozen at their initial value while the comment says they are averaged, and `current_thickness_buffer()` returns the input of the last sub-step (one sub-step stale). Lead-confirmed: `rg 'set_dt\('` finds only the definition at `src/render/gpu_drainage.rs:391`.
acceptance: `params.dt` written every frame (`queue.write_buffer`) with a CFL-limited sub-step count; `current_time` advances by the time actually integrated
Per-step thickness increments are representable in f32 (store the deviation from h0 or a nondimensional thickness), or the initial field is non-uniform
Pole rows handled by a zero-flux finite-volume form or ring averaging, with comments matching the code
The thickness accessor returns the buffer written last; the caustic bind group uses the same current buffer
A headless GPU test (may be `#[ignore]`) asserts the thickness field changes after N steps and stays finite and non-negative

groups.title: [HIGH] Drainage: CPU solver instability, non-conservative PDE, unbounded TFE decay, config not propagated
groups.summary: Enabling CPU drainage (off by default) runs one forward-Euler step per frame with dt = frame_dt x 100, about 1.67 s at 60 fps, roughly 14x over the explicit phi-diffusion limit at the first ring off the pole (0.115 s); numpy and Rust replicas blow up near both poles within about 25 frames. The gravity term `-rho g h^3 / (3 eta) * sin(theta)` is a flux used as a rate: wrong units, a mass sink everywhere, and symmetric about the equator, so the bottom never thickens. The 'TFE ratio 0.85 (Monier 2025)' is applied as unbounded exponential decay that goes negative for dt > 13.3 s. The Marangoni coupling is one-signed with inconsistent units. `SimulationConfig` and CLI parameters never reach either drainage solver. At 500 nm the physical terms barely act, so the visible dynamics come from the ad-hoc TFE sink. The GPU solver shares the PDE form, so fixes should land in both (see {#gpu-drainage}).
acceptance: Frame dt clamped and integrated with CFL-limited sub-steps, or the phi-diffusion treated implicitly (periodic tridiagonal solve per latitude ring)
Gravity drainage in conservative finite-volume flux form on sin-weighted theta faces with zero flux through the poles; a test asserts mass conservation
Thin-film elements implemented as a bounded relaxation towards ratio x adjacent thickness, stable for any dt
Marangoni term in consistent SI units, or explicitly documented as a stylised effect
`SimulationConfig` (radius, thickness, fluid parameters) reaches both drainage solvers
A test runs the CPU solver for 1000 frames at default settings at 60 fps and 10 fps and asserts finite, non-negative thickness

groups.title: [HIGH] Branched flow: GRIN bending is dead (thickness_scale unused) and caustics output a constant
groups.summary: `thickness_scale` (1e6) is declared at `src/render/shaders/branched_flow_compute.wgsl:38` and set at `src/render/branched_flow.rs:128` but never read in the shader. Gradients are taken on metre-valued thickness (about 5e-7), so a full ray deflects by about 2e-4 degrees: all visible branching comes from the scatterers, and the 'GRIN bending' slider effectively scales the particle force. `caustics_compute.wgsl` has the same unit bug and outputs 2.0 everywhere. Physically the GRIN coefficient is grad ln n_eff(d) for the slab waveguide, which varies about 40x with thickness. Further sampling defects: u and v differences weighted 1:1 although u spans 2 pi and v spans pi, the phi wrap is ignored, the sampler's phi grid convention differs from the drainage grid, and the seam texels are double-counted. Lead-confirmed: `thickness_scale` appears in the shader only in the struct declaration. Without {#gpu-drainage} fixed, the field is flat anyway.
acceptance: Thickness sampled in consistent units (apply `thickness_scale` or store nm) and `bend_strength` retuned
Ray force uses grad ln n_eff(d) from a CPU-built lookup table, or a documented scaling at the base thickness
Gradient uses the sphere metric: d/du divided by (2 pi sin theta), d/dv divided by pi
Thickness sampling wraps phi periodically with the drainage grid's convention (delta phi = 2 pi / W); seam texels are not double-counted
`caustics_compute.wgsl` uses the same units and its output varies with the thickness field
A CPU replica or headless test shows non-zero GRIN deflection for a known gradient

groups.title: [HIGH] Branched flow: patch view renders 180 degrees away from the simulated patch
groups.summary: `SpherePatch::generate_mesh_indexed` maps u to azimuth with phi = 2 pi u (u = 0.5 at -x), while both shaders use u = (atan2(z, x) + pi) / (2 pi) (u = 0.5 at +x). The two conventions are half a turn apart, so the default-on patch view never shows branched flow; full-sphere mode is unaffected. Lead-confirmed: `src/physics/geometry.rs:411` vs `src/render/shaders/bubble.wgsl:236-240`. Hidden behind it: the patch-mode spawn offset uses a chord projection instead of the gnomonic inverse and the default patch centre lies on the entry point's gnomonic horizon, so only a thin strip would light up once the 180-degree bug is fixed. The gnomonic chart also distorts deposit density off-centre, the beam direction degenerates at some entry points, and the deformation slider does not regenerate the patch mesh.
acceptance: One longitude convention shared by mesh generation and shaders; a unit test pushes patch-mesh normals through the shader UV mapping and asserts they land inside the patch window
Patch-mode spawning uses the gnomonic inverse or a chart centred on the patch, and the default entry point and patch are consistent so the patch is substantially lit
(Optional) exponential-map propagation on the sphere; this changes the propagation loop body, so test with small ray counts on a hardware adapter first
Beam direction defined in the local tangent frame, with no degenerate entry points
`set_deformation` regenerates the patch mesh

groups.title: [HIGH] Branched flow: sampling quality (biased scatterer drift, frame-invariant seeds, pinned step, deposit truncation)
groups.summary: The scatterer 'Brownian' perturbation is a sign-preserving `fract()` hash of `film_time` with a mean of -0.0005 UV per frame, so scatterers pile into the patch corner within about 10 s (or the pole and seam in full-sphere mode), emptying the region the beam crosses; with the film paused they drift ballistically. Ray seeds depend only on `ray_idx`, so the 0.85 fade re-traces identical paths (6.7x brightness, no new samples), and `hash21` yields about 26% duplicate seeds at 65,536 rays. The adaptive step is pinned at its 0.3 floor in 97-99% of steps, which cuts range 3.3x. The x64 fixed-point deposits lose 53-62% of their energy to truncation. The spatial hash truncates forces when the radius slider exceeds about 0.033. These directly undercut the uncommitted 32K -> 8K ray default change, whose comments claim accumulation fills in density and adaptive stepping extends range.
acceptance: Scatterer perturbation is zero-mean (seeded RNG or frame counter), does not drift while paused, and wraps u in full-sphere mode
Ray seeds vary per frame through an integer hash (e.g. PCG of `ray_idx ^ frame * 0x9E3779B9`); a test shows no duplicate seeds at 64K rays
Step size controlled by turning angle (or step/range retuned) and falloff applied per unit length; this touches the loop body, so test small first on a hardware adapter
Deposit fixed-point scale raised (>= 1024) or stochastic rounding used; a test ties the encode and decode constants together
Spatial-hash search radius covers 3 sigma_max, or the radius slider is clamped
Default ray count and its code comments reflect the corrected behaviour

groups.title: [HIGH] Stability: wgpu validation panics, local lib-suite segfault, red CI
groups.summary: Two wgpu validation panics are reachable from the UI or on real GPUs, and the test and CI infrastructure currently cannot signal regressions: locally a driver crash aborts the whole lib test binary, and CI has been red on Clippy and Format since March.
lead_findings: [HIGH] Local `cargo test` aborts with SIGSEGV in `render::headless::tests::test_headless_pipeline_creation` (`src/render/headless.rs:516`, not `#[ignore]`d) whenever the Mesa Dozen Vulkan ICD is visible. Measured by ICD bisection: Dozen only -> exit 139; lavapipe only or no Vulkan ICD -> pass; GL forced to llvmpipe -> still exit 139, so the crash is in the wgpu-24 Vulkan path over Dozen (debug build). One crash kills all 136 lib tests. Workaround: `scripts/test-local.sh` (forces the lavapipe ICD). Probe: `scripts/gpu/probe-adapters.sh`.

[MEDIUM] CI red since 2026-03-10: on the last `main` push (run 22917111076) and on PR #40 (run 32022056203), Check and Test pass but Clippy and Format fail. Local `cargo clippy --all-targets` reports 7 warnings.
acceptance: `set_msaa_samples` rebuilds every pipeline (bubble, instanced, wall, caustic) for the new sample count
`GpuProfiler` skips resolve and copy while a readback is pending (or rotates 2-3 readback buffers) and resolves only queries written this frame, or is replaced by the `wgpu-profiler` crate
(Optional) an `on_uncaptured_error` handler logs instead of panicking in release builds
The headless GPU test is gated (`#[ignore]` or an adapter allow-list) so a driver crash cannot abort the lib suite
CI green: `cargo fmt` applied and clippy warnings fixed

groups.title: [HIGH] Foam: integrator stability and physics model (inertia, buoyancy, Plateau, wall curvature, sampling)
groups.summary: `FoamSimulator::step` treats drag, contact springs and adhesion explicitly with film-only mass (19-37x too little inertia) and water viscosity. At frame dt it is unstable, so bubbles jitter 1.67 mm per frame at the 0.1 m/s velocity clamp indefinitely. Buoyancy omits the enclosed gas, so net gravity clamps to zero for R > 1.25 mm. Plateau's laws are claimed but not enforced (contact equilibrium gives about 36/162 degree angles). The shared-wall curvature radius is half the physical value and bulges into the smaller bubble. Size distributions are clamped rather than truncated (up to 64% of radii pile up on the bounds), the 'HCP' generator has coordination 6, and gravity deformation is not volume-conserving, with dead Bond-number helpers.
acceptance: Physical effective mass (film + enclosed gas + added mass), air viscosity, implicit drag, `exp(-c dt)` damping and smooth adhesion; a test shows a perturbed cluster relaxes to rest without hitting the velocity clamp
Net weight `m_film * g` acts downward; test
Wall radius `1 / |1/Ra - 1/Rb|` with the apex toward the larger bubble; test
Plateau geometry enforced, or the stylised contact model documented (ties into #16)
Size sampling truncates by rejection or inverse CDF; random positions use uniform sphere sampling
HCP lattice has coordination 12 (test) and `spacing` means nearest-neighbour distance for every lattice
Deformation is volume-conserving or documented as stylised; dead Bond-number code is removed or used

groups.title: [MEDIUM] Optics: interference LUT precision, CIE fit and spectral sampling
groups.summary: Once the phase is fixed ({#airy-phase}), colour accuracy is limited by how the LUT is built. 8-bit linear storage of values <= 0.04 leaves about 9-10 code values on the normal-incidence row (contouring). The CIE Gaussian fit drops Wyman 2013's asymmetric sigmas and no illuminant is applied, so a flat spectrum renders orange (1, 0.76, 0.43). Seven samples at 50 nm alias (Delta E 6.5 at 500 nm, 19-31 above about 1.1 um). The foam shader evaluates its own 7-sample spectrum per fragment instead of sampling the LUT. Belcour & Barla 2017 is the state-of-the-art reference for antialiased iridescence.
acceptance: LUT stored as `Rgba16Float` (or normalised / sRGB-encoded 8-bit with rounding)
LUT built from tabulated CIE 1931 2-degree CMFs weighted by D65 at <= 5 nm steps (or the restored asymmetric Wyman fit plus D65); a white reflector renders neutral (test)
LUT lookups address texel centres
`bubble_instanced.wgsl` samples the shared LUT instead of the inline 7-sample loop

groups.title: [MEDIUM] Rendering: shading-model defects (drainage gradient, wall optics, compositing, export colours)
groups.summary: Independent of the phase bug ({#airy-phase}). The procedural drainage gradient is upside down: the film is thinnest at the bottom with +Y up, while the code comment and README say the top drains faster. `wall.wgsl` renders the Airy transmission term as reflected colour, so walls come out near-white. Polarisation is averaged before the Airy formula instead of after (up to 7.7% error at oblique angles). A hard 30 nm black-film cutoff creates a brightness step and becomes redundant once the phase is fixed. Compositing is opacity-style alpha instead of reflection plus transmission. Screenshots swap R and B unconditionally. The instanced-bubble normal correction cancels itself.
acceptance: Drainage gradient uses `(1 + normal.y)` (or samples the drainage buffer) in both bubble shaders; code comment and README agree
`wall.wgsl` uses the reflectance form, ideally via the shared LUT
The LUT generator evaluates Airy separately for Rs and Rp, then averages
The 30 nm cutoff is removed or turned into an explicit rupture/opacity effect
Compositing choice (physical premultiplied R/T vs artistic alpha) made and documented
Screenshot R/B swap applied only for BGRA surface formats
Instanced-bubble normal transform correct for non-uniform scale, or simplified with a comment

groups.title: [MEDIUM] Performance: branched-flow force field, recording stalls, bind-group caching, build profiles
groups.summary: All figures are estimates; there are no hardware timings yet (#38). Ray-step cost is dominated by the scatterer loop: about 163-170 scatterers are visited per step in patch mode (the docs say 10-30). Precomputing a per-frame force-field grid (GRIN gradient plus scatterer forces) is expected to cut per-step work about 10-25x. Recording mode calls `poll(Wait)` and joins the previous PNG encode every captured frame. The per-frame bind-group rebuild can be replaced by two cached groups, and drainage's 10 passes can share one compute pass. Dev builds leave dependencies unoptimised. CPU-side per-frame work was measured at 17 us (scatterer perturb + sort + prefix-sum, n = 400), so no rayon work is justified yet. Measurement is blocked on {#stability} (GpuProfiler race) and on a hardware adapter (#38).
acceptance: A force-field compute pass runs before the trace and the trace samples it; this changes the loop body, so test with small ray counts on a hardware adapter first; before/after measured with GpuProfiler
Recording uses 2-3 staging buffers and a persistent encoder thread with fast PNG compression
Two cached bind groups replace the per-frame rebuild; drainage sub-steps share one compute pass
`[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 3` added; release-profile choice (fat vs thin LTO) measured

groups.summary: **Audit 2026-10-09 status update.** The 0.85 fade in `branched_flow_compute.wgsl:556-569` already implements the recurrence S <- 0.85 S + D, an exponential moving average with a 6.7-frame window; the double buffer proposed here computes the same recurrence. However, ray seeds depend only on `ray_idx`, so every frame re-traces identical paths and the accumulation adds brightness, not samples. That defect is tracked in {#ray-sampling}. Suggest re-scoping this issue to 'per-frame seeds + expose the fade factor + clear on laser/patch parameter change', or closing it in favour of {#ray-sampling}.

**Audit 2026-10-09 status update.** Per-workgroup shared-memory privatisation is not viable as written: deposits scatter randomly across the 512x256 texture, so a workgroup tile would catch few of its own rays' deposits, and atomics are estimated at about 0.15 ms on a discrete GPU. The viable variant is subgroup-aggregated deposits (`Features::SUBGROUP` already exists in wgpu 24), attempted only after profiling on hardware shows atomics on the profile. Suggest closing, or re-scoping after the force-field work in {#perf}.

**Audit 2026-10-09 status update.** Workgroup size is the wrong lever: 8192 rays is 128 workgroups of 64, about 12% occupancy on the RTX 3070 Ti Laptop GPU (46 SMs); 128- or 256-wide groups would leave SMs idle at this ray count. Suggest keeping `@workgroup_size(64)` and re-scoping to 'ray-count scaling per adapter type' (e.g. 8K on CPU rasterisers, 32K+ on discrete GPUs). See also the subgroup note on #36 and {#perf}.

**Audit 2026-10-09 status update: premise partly stale (measured).** With Mesa 26.0.5 (kisak PPA) installed, `vulkaninfo --summary` lists Dozen (Vulkan 1.2 over D3D12) adapters for the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti Laptop GPU and the AMD iGPU, plus llvmpipe. wgpu hides the Dozen adapters (`Adapter is not Vulkan compliant, hiding adapter: Microsoft Direct3D12 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti Laptop GPU)`), and the app now runs on the Vulkan backend over lavapipe (CPU), not GLES. `WGPU_ALLOW_UNDERLYING_NONCOMPLIANT_ADAPTER` has no effect because neither `pipeline.rs:284` nor `headless.rs:56` builds its instance flags with `.with_env()`. Cheapest route to hardware: `flags: wgpu::InstanceFlags::from_build_config().with_env()` plus `PowerPreference::HighPerformance`, and log `adapter.get_info()`. Caveats: Dozen is non-conformant, and a debug-build headless test segfaults when Dozen is visible (tracked in {#stability}); a native Windows build is the robust fallback. `scripts/gpu/probe-adapters.sh` reproduces the probe. Upgrading wgpu 24 -> 30 does not change the non-compliant-adapter gate, and moving compute to CUDA is not recommended (no graphics interop on WSL).

**Audit 2026-10-09 status update.** Blocked: the compute shader's GRIN term is currently scaled to about zero because `thickness_scale` is never applied, and the GPU drainage field never changes, so noise modulations would perturb a gradient that does not act on the rays. Fix {#grin-units} and {#gpu-drainage} first.
